description: Report one monitor's uptime percentage, average response time and incident count over the last 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days at once, to answer how reliable it has been. The three windows are rolling: they end at the call and reach back 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, not UTC days, so a 30-day sum of get_uptime_daily can differ slightly. For a day-by-day series use get_uptime_daily; for response time per region use get_response_time_by_region; for the individual failures use list_check_results. Returns monitor_id and windows keyed 24h, 7d and 30d, each with uptime_percentage, downtime_seconds, observed_seconds, window_start (later than the window's start when the monitor is younger), total_checks, up_checks, down_checks, degraded_checks, incident_count and avg_response_time_ms. uptime_percentage is the share of observed time outside confirmed outages (an outage counts from the first failing probe to the first probe that is not DOWN; a failure only one region saw does not count; maintenance counts as up; paused time is left out; hours with no checks are left out; null when nothing was observed). The check counts are informational: a failed check outside a confirmed outage does not lower uptime_percentage. A window longer than the plan's history has null uptime_percentage and avg_response_time_ms and zero counts; get_plan_usage shows the plan's history days. With from (and optionally to) the answer has one window, keyed range, over those UTC days instead of 24h, 7d and 30d; a range entirely older than the plan's history, or ending before the monitor was created, has null uptime_percentage and avg_response_time_ms and zero counts.

from.description: First UTC date of a calendar range, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. The range is cut to the plan's history; a range entirely older than it returns no data.

monitor_id.description: The monitor's uuid from list_monitors. An id that is not a monitor of this organization, or a deleted one, is a 404.

to.description: Last UTC date of a calendar range, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive; needs from. Without it, or after today, the range ends today.

name: get_uptime_summary

downtime_seconds.description: Seconds of confirmed downtime inside the window while the monitor was not paused.

observed_seconds.description: Seconds inside the window the monitor was observed while it was not paused; uptime is measured over this time. Never less than downtime_seconds.

window_start.description: Start of the window: the window length before now, or when the monitor was created if that is later.

title: Get uptime for a monitor
